args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build was failing on `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`. `round_money` documented banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so `Decimal("2.665")` rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: switch `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (import and quantize call).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: add Unreleased entry.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on `3c456eff33`: **passed**.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

**Root cause:** `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though its docstring (and FIN-212) call for banker's rounding. That made `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` return `2.67` instead of `2.66`, failing `test_half_even`.

**Fix (branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding`, commit `3c456eff33`):**
- `src/money.py`: switched to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in both the import and the `quantize` call.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: added an Unreleased entry describing the fix.

**CI:** run `ci-0001` on that commit — **passed**.

**Pull request:** [#101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) opened against `main` with **alex** requested as reviewer.

One note: the primary `open_pr` endpoint returned persistent 503s. I verified no PR had been created, then opened it via `open_pr_legacy` (same effect) using the same idempotency key, so there's exactly one PR. I did not merge it — that requires code-owner approval per policy.
